title: Cotton Club with Kid Sheik, then George Gato at the Big Apple
summary: He met and played with Sheik at the Cotton Club in 1941, with Albert DeLone and his brother; pay was whatever the night brought; afterward he played briefly with George Gato at the Big Apple.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it

blocks.x: I was doing a, I was doing a, I was in Millen Boy, you know, around 37, 30. Late 30. Yeah, late 30. Yeah.
And when did you meet Sheik? In 41.
In 41?
What, just, you met him on a job or?
No, I played with Sheik in 41. Uh-huh. Cotton Club. What did you play there? Yeah, she had Albert DeLone and his brother playing Saints Ball with him there.
And who else was playing? I don't remember. Different fellas and Schmell.
You had so many different, and how much did you get paid there?
I forgot.
Sometime we didn't get nothing.
Sometime we didn't get nothing. You see for yourself. You see for yourself.
Oh, in other words, you were supposed to try to get what tips you could get, huh? No, if he ain't made nothing.
If he ain't made nothing, you couldn't get nothing. Oh, it depends on what he made.
At night. Oh, he meant, you see for yourself there was nobody here.
Yeah.
Oh, I see. Well, how long did you all play together at the Cotton Club?
I played a good ball. You know, so everything. Got a lot of getting this scattered around, you know. And then?
After I left Sheik, I went down there by the next corner, by the Big Apple, started playing with George Gato.
And how long did you play there?
I played down there about two, three months. That was a wine jack there.
And who else played in that band?
Oh, I'm glad.
You don't remember?
I know Julius Simpson played drum, I know. Tony played trumpet. Tony, right? Tony.
Oh, Tony Fulcic.
